newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOWLER AND MATTEO OF LIVERPOOL INJURED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOWLER AND MATTEO OF LIVERPOOL INJURED.

text.p: Liverpool's Robbie Fowler and Dominic Matteo have lost their respective battles to play in England's World Cup qualifying match against Poland at Wembley on Wednesday.
The two have returned to Liverpool for further treatment on injuries that kept them out of new manager Glenn Hoddle's early training sessions.
It is the second successive match that striker Fowler, who has an ankle problem, has been ruled out of Hoddle's plans.
Defender Matteo, 22, was called up for the match to cap a meteoric rise this season but his dream has been shattered by a persistent knee injury.
Hoddle, however, has ruled out calling for replacements just three days before the group two match, happy that he has adequate cover from within the remaining 21 members of his squad.
He believes his side can now take prime position in the group after rivals Italy could only beat Moldova 3-1 on Saturday.
While England meet Poland, Arrigo Sacchi's side will complete a double-header at home to dark horses Georgia.
And their failure to match England's 3-0 scoreline in Kishinev is a big boost.

"I thought the Italians were always going to win because of Moldova's frailties," Hoddle said after watching a satellite clip of the game that was decided by Middlesbrough striker Fabrizio Ravanelli's double.
"But the storm they faced lasted longer than it did for us and many of the best passing movements came from Moldova.
"It was a bit of an eye-opener that the Italians struggled for significant periods."
Most of the England squad played golf on Sunday but Hoddle took the opportunity to have head-to-head chats with several of his big names, notably Paul Gascoigne.
"He is much fitter than when he played in Moldova and I've been impressed by his will to win and his excellent attitude in training," Hoddle said.
"I've told him he is still in his prime and, as he found in 1990, the World Cup is a wonderful stage on which he can still star."
